newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end with modest gain after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end with modest gain after rate cut.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended modestly higher on Monday after investors used another round of interest cuts by the Bank of Canada and the country's big chartered banks to take profits.
The TSE 300 Composite Index edged up 3.58 points to close at 5553.36 in turnover of 81.68 million shares worth C$1.23 billion ($743 million).
The Bank of Canada earlier today cut its key bank rate to 3.50 percent from 3.75 percent, the lowest short-term interest rates in Canada in 33 years.
Canada's major chartered banks quickly lowered their prime lending rates to 5.0 percent from 5.25 percent, the lowest level since July 1956.
The rate moves were widely anticipated during the past two weeks and factored into the market, analysts said.

"Stocks have run up in anticipation and now that the news is out -- based on the theory of buy on mystery and sell on history -- I think that people are selling on history," said Ron Meisels, president of Montreal-based P & C Holdings Ltd.
Economists said rates may have room to go lower, provided U.S. interest rates remain steady and the Canadian dollar continues to strengthen.
The latest rate reduction was the 10th this year and the 19th since Canada's central bank began cutting in May 1995 to spur a sluggish Canadian economy.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce chairman Al Flood said his bank saw signs that the rate cuts were having an effect and rates are close to bottoming out.
"These are very good rates. I think we're getting near the bottom. I would suggest we might see some further movement, but very little," Flood told reporters after a speech.
In today's action on the TSE, communications and conglomerates led 10 of 14 groups higher. Banks and base metals led the weak side.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 499 to 474 with 280 issues unchanged.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. jumped 3.45 to 24.25 on 7.04 million shares after the gold miner moved to resolve a dispute over its huge Busang discovery in Indonesia.
Bre-X unveiled an alliance with a company controlled by the son of Indonesian president Suharto.
* Tarxien Corp. gained 1.45 to 13.95 after the company recommended shareholders accept a C$14.10 ($10.50) a share offer from Gecamex Technologies Inc.
* Airline operator Transat A.T. lead weak issues, off 2.20 to end at 28.
* Bank stocks suffered modest profit taking after enjoying a strong run since July.
CIBC fell 0.55 to 54.05, while Bank of Montreal dipped 0.35 to 40.25. Royal Bank of Canada bucked the trend, edging up 0.05 to 43.05.
